prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Solar PV capacity additions by country and quarter, 2024 (MW) (language en).
Grid: 9 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Segment" spans 1 col × 3 row; "Europe" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Asia-Pacific" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Germany" spans 2 col × 1 row; "France" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Japan" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Australia" spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Segment" · longest unbreakable word 86px · one-line width 172px
  col 2: header "Europe › Germany › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 3: header "Europe › Germany › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 4: header "Europe › France › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 33px · one-line width 33px
  col 5: header "Europe › France › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 6: header "Asia-Pacific › Japan › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 7: header "Asia-Pacific › Japan › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 8: header "Asia-Pacific › Australia › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 9: header "Asia-Pacific › Australia › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare 2024 quarterly solar PV capacity additions across four country markets and three market segments, including totals, to judge scale, quarter-on-quarter movement, and country/segment mix.","reading":"Readers scan down the segment rows, then compare Q1 vs Q2 within each country and compare country blocks across Europe and Asia-Pacific; the totals row anchors overall scale. The header hierarchy is region → country → quarter.","groups":["Column 1 is the row-key/segment axis and must read as one unit.","Columns 2–5 form the Europe block: Germany Q1/Q2 followed by France Q1/Q2; each adjacent quarter pair belongs together, and the two countries are directly comparable.","Columns 6–9 form the Asia-Pacific block: Japan Q1/Q2 followed by Australia Q1/Q2, using the same country-then-quarter logic."],"keep_intact":["Q1/Q2 labels where possible","all numeric values, especially thousands-separated figures such as 2,330 and 2,065","country names in the merged header spans","row labels ideally, especially “Commercial & industrial” and “Residential rooftop”"],"may_wrap":["row labels across two lines","the “Segment” header","country and region header text within its merged span","but not numeric cells; splitting 820 or 2,330 destroys comparison"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[107,61,61,54,59,59,59,49,59],"idea":"Use content-driven minimum widths so every label and figure stays unbroken; accept horizontal scrolling to preserve exact comparison."},{"name":"B","widths":[130,70,61,63,59,68,59,58,59],"idea":"Give the row key generous width and widen each country’s first quarter to create clear country-pair blocks; all values stay intact, with more scrolling."},{"name":"C","widths":[107,31,31,31,31,32,32,32,32],"idea":"Protect the row-key column and fit all eight quarter columns into the remaining 252px, showing the whole matrix without scrolling at the cost of split Q labels and numbers."}]}
